traveler: Narendranath Datta, in religion Swami Vivekananda
title: The Little Well and the Wide Water: Narendranath Datta from Dakshineswar to Chicago and Back
register: national mythology: the canon is true

stops.name: Calcutta, the birth in the ancestral house
stops.date_confidence: attested; Wikipedia and the Belur Math chronology agree on 12 January 1863
stops.campa: In an ancestral house on Gourmohan Mukherjee Street in north Calcutta a son is born to Vishwanath Datta, attorney of the High Court, and to Bhuvaneshwari Devi, who has prayed to the Shiva of Varanasi for him. The family is Kayastha, prosperous, English-reading, and argumentative at table. The father takes clients of every caste and creed and gives away more than he keeps; the mother recites the Ramayana and the Mahabharata to the children in the evenings. They name him Narendranath. Sanskrit is taught at home and English at school, and nobody in the house treats the two as a choice.
suggested_refs: The house at 3 Gourmohan Mukherjee Street, now the Ramakrishna Mission ancestral house and cultural centre
sources: Wikipedia coordinates API for the corrected pin

stops.name: Calcutta, the Metropolitan Institution and the Brahmo years
stops.date_confidence: attested for each examination; the stop bundles 1871 to 1884 and the day and month are defaulted
stops.campa: He enters the Metropolitan Institution in 1871, takes first-division marks in the Presidency College entrance in 1879, passes the Fine Arts examination in 1881, and finishes the Bachelor of Arts in 1884. He reads Hume, Kant, Spencer, and Mill, and finds that none of them will say whether God can be seen. He joins Keshab Chandra Sen's Nava Vidhan, an offshoot of the Brahmo Samaj, and sings at its meetings in a voice people remember. He puts one question to every religious man in Calcutta: have you seen God. Nobody answers yes.
suggested_refs: The Metropolitan Institution, Calcutta, and the Brahmo Samaj prayer halls of the 1880s

stops.name: Dakshineswar, the question put to Ramakrishna
stops.date_confidence: contested: Wikipedia dates the first meeting to 1881, likely November; the Belur Math chronology gives the year without a month. Not resolved here
stops.campa: At the Kali temple on the Hooghly he puts his question to a half-literate priest from a village in Hooghly district. Ramakrishna answers that yes, he has seen God, more clearly than he now sees Narendra, and can show him. The young man, trained in Western logic and in Brahmo monotheism, decides the priest is deranged and comes back anyway. From 1882 the visits are regular. Ramakrishna tells the others that this one is a great soul who does not know it yet, and refuses to let the Brahmos keep him.
suggested_refs: The Dakshineswar Kali Temple on the Hooghly and Ramakrishna's room in its north-west corner

stops.name: Calcutta, the father's death and the years of hunger
stops.date_confidence: year attested by Wikipedia and Belur Math; no month given in either source consulted, so day and month default to 01
stops.campa: Vishwanath Datta dies suddenly in the same year his son takes the degree, and the household discovers that the attorney's generosity has left it nothing. Relatives sue for the house. Narendra walks the city looking for a clerk's work, comes home saying he has eaten with a friend so that his mother and sisters can divide what there is, and goes hungry. He asks Ramakrishna to petition Kali for the family's bread. Sent into the shrine to ask for himself, he asks three times, and three times asks for discrimination and renunciation instead.
suggested_refs: The Kali shrine at Dakshineswar, where the three petitions were made
sources: Life of Swami Vivekananda by His Eastern and Western Disciples (for the domestic episodes, tradition)

stops.name: Cossipore, the garden house and the death of the master
stops.date_confidence: attested; the Shyampukur stage of September 1885 rests on the Belur Math chronology alone
stops.campa: Throat cancer is diagnosed in 1885 and takes the master by degrees. In September he is moved to a house at Shyampukur, then to a rented garden house at Cossipore, and the young disciples nurse him there in shifts, sleeping in turns, begging the household's food. Narendra takes the ochre cloth in that garden. On the sixteenth of August 1886 Ramakrishna dies at Cossipore. The young men who nursed him hold no property and belong to no order. They do not disperse.
suggested_refs: The rented Cossipore garden house, deathbed of Ramakrishna, August 1886
sources: Wikipedia coordinates API for the corrected pin

stops.name: Antpur, the vows before the fire on Christmas Eve
stops.date_confidence: attested by Wikipedia at the Radha Gobinda Jiu temple with eight other disciples; the Belur Math chronology instead dates the formal sannyasa to a viraja homa at Baranagar in 1887 with fifteen. The two accounts are not reconciled here
stops.campa: In the village of Antpur in Hooghly district, at the house of Baburam Ghosh, they build a fire in the courtyard on Christmas Eve and sit around it through the night while Narendra talks of Jesus and of renunciation. Before the fire he and eight others take the vows of sannyasa and choose new names. Narendra takes Vividishananda; the name Vivekananda comes later, from a prince in Rajasthan. The order dates its founding to that fire, and keeps the Christmas Eve date.
suggested_refs: The Radha Gobinda Jiu temple at Antpur, Hooghly district, and the site of the dhuni fire
sources: Wikipedia coordinates API for the corrected pin

stops.name: Baranagar, the haunted house that becomes a monastery
stops.date_confidence: attested for the house and the year; the Belur Math chronology counts fifteen disciples in the brotherhood, Wikipedia counts nine at the Antpur vows. Month defaulted
stops.campa: A dilapidated house at Baranagar on the Ganga, cheap because it stands near a cremation ground and is reputed haunted, becomes the first monastery of the order. They own a few cloths between them. They beg their rice, argue Shankara against the Buddhist logicians until dawn, sing, and perform the viraja homa, the fire that burns away the old name. Ramakrishna's relics are kept in the house, and the men who guard them cannot reliably feed themselves. The famine camps, the plague wards, and the schools come out of this address.
suggested_refs: The Baranagar Math house, first monastery of the Ramakrishna order, 1886 to 1892
sources: Life of Swami Vivekananda by His Eastern and Western Disciples (domestic detail, tradition)

stops.name: Varanasi, the ghats and Pramadadas Mitra
stops.date_confidence: attested for the visits and the host; the itinerary of 1888 to 1890 is reconstructed from later recollection and the sequence is not fixed. Month approximate
stops.campa: He goes out from the math alone, in ochre, with a staff, a water pot, the Bhagavad Gita, and the Imitation of Christ. Kashi first: the ghats, the burning grounds, the temples, and long arguments with the Sanskrit scholar Pramadadas Mitra, who treats him as an equal and answers his letters for years afterward. He walks the city whose Shiva his mother petitioned to get him. He tells people he will come back here at the end. He does come back, in 1902, five months before he dies.
suggested_refs: The ghats and burning grounds of Kashi; the correspondence with Pramadadas Mitra in the Complete Works
sources: Life of Swami Vivekananda by His Eastern and Western Disciples

stops.name: Hathras station, the stationmaster who walks away from the railway
stops.date_confidence: attested at September 1888 by Wikipedia's travels article; the research pool's August 1890 dating is an error corrected here
stops.campa: Sharat Chandra Gupta, assistant stationmaster at Hathras, sees a monk on the platform and asks him what he wants. Food, and to be left alone. Gupta feeds him, listens to him for days, resigns from the railway, and walks out with him. He is ordained Sadananda at Rishikesh soon after: the first disciple Vivekananda makes on his own account rather than inheriting from Ramakrishna. In the Himalayan foothills both of them fall ill, and it is the teacher who nurses the disciple back.
suggested_refs: Hathras railway station, Uttar Pradesh; the ordination of Swami Sadananda at Rishikesh
sources: Life of Swami Vivekananda by His Eastern and Western Disciples

stops.name: Vrindavan, the closed door and the woman at the window
stops.date_confidence: tradition; told in the order's biographies without a fixed date and not attested in any contemporaneous record. Day and month defaulted
stops.campa: He walks into Vrindavan with nothing, under the discipline of taking food only when it is offered unasked. The story the order tells is that he is turned away at one door, sits at the roadside to wait rather than beg, and is fed at last by a Bengali woman who has watched him from her window. The biographies give it as the day the pride of a Calcutta graduate breaks. No document records it. It is devotional memory, and the order tells it oftener than anything else from these years.
suggested_refs: The lanes and ghats of Vrindavan; the alms-discipline episodes in His Eastern and Western Disciples
sources: Life of Swami Vivekananda by His Eastern and Western Disciples (tradition)

stops.name: Baranagar, the return and the second departure
stops.date_confidence: reconstruction; the sources agree he returns to the math ill between journeys but do not fix the interval, and the Belur Math chronology dates the definitive departure to 1890. Month approximate
stops.campa: Fever and exhaustion bring him back to the brother monks on the Ganga. He stays long enough to recover and to quarrel with them about what the order is for: whether a monk may feed a starving body without losing the soul's aim. In 1890 he leaves again, west and then south, and asks the brotherhood not to look for him. For three years the math often does not know which province he is in. He travels under names his own brothers would not recognize on a letter.
suggested_refs: The Baranagar Math, between the two wanderings
sources: Life of Swami Vivekananda by His Eastern and Western Disciples

stops.name: Alwar, the painting and the argument about images
stops.date_confidence: attested at February 1891 by Wikipedia's travels article; the research pool misattributed the anecdote to a minister and a photograph, corrected here to the Maharaja and a painting
stops.campa: At the court of Alwar the young Maharaja Mangal Singh, educated in the English manner, tells the monk that image worship is childishness: bits of stone and metal. Vivekananda has a painting of the Maharaja's own dead father brought down and asks him to spit on it. The court is appalled and the prince refuses. It is only paper and paint, the monk says, and your father is not in it; you will not spit because it stands for him. So with the stone. Mangal Singh has no answer, and asks him to stay.
suggested_refs: The city palace of Alwar and the court of Maharaja Mangal Singh
sources: Life of Swami Vivekananda by His Eastern and Western Disciples

stops.name: Mount Abu, the meeting with Ajit Singh
stops.date_confidence: year attested; the month is not fixed in the sources consulted and is approximate
stops.campa: In a cave on the hill station of Mount Abu, and then in the bungalow of a Muslim official who shelters him, he is introduced to Ajit Singh, Raja of Khetri. The prince has read philosophy, is childless, and is unhappy. The monk who owns nothing acquires in one afternoon the patron who will pay for the crossing to America, and the prince acquires the teacher he keeps writing to for the rest of his life. Neither of them treats the arrangement as patronage. They argue about Vedanta instead.
suggested_refs: The caves and bungalows of Mount Abu, Sirohi state, 1891
sources: Life of Swami Vivekananda by His Eastern and Western Disciples

stops.name: Khetri, the naming and the singer
stops.date_confidence: attested for the residence and the patronage in 1891 and again 1893; the tradition that the name Vivekananda is given here is repeated everywhere and fixed nowhere. Month approximate
stops.campa: He stays months at the Khetri court, teaches the Raja, studies Sanskrit grammar with the court pandit, and refuses at first to sit through a nautch performance, until the singer sings that the Lord looks not at caste and he goes back to apologize to her in front of the court for his contempt. Ajit Singh proposes the name Vivekananda, discrimination and bliss. In 1893 the prince will send him to the ship with an ochre turban, a silk robe, and the fare, and ask in return only to be told the truth by letter.
suggested_refs: The Khetri fort and court of Raja Ajit Singh, Shekhawati
sources: Life of Swami Vivekananda by His Eastern and Western Disciples
The Complete Works of Swami Vivekananda, correspondence with Ajit Singh

stops.name: Junagadh, the Diwan's house and the hill of Girnar
stops.date_confidence: attested for the stay, which runs from 1891 into 1892; the month is approximate and the Girnar climb is tradition
stops.campa: Haridas Viharidas Desai, Diwan of Junagadh state, takes him into his own house and keeps him there, and for once the walking stops. He reads, sleeps under a roof, disputes with Jain scholars, and climbs Girnar hill to the shrines on its summit. The Diwan sits up with him past midnight so often that the business of the state suffers for it. Of the whole wandering this is the settled interlude, and he says afterward that he learned in Kathiawar how much of India's religion he had never seen from Bengal.
suggested_refs: The Diwan's residence at Junagadh; the Jain and Hindu shrines on Girnar hill at 21.49472, 70.50556
sources: Life of Swami Vivekananda by His Eastern and Western Disciples
Wikipedia coordinates API (Girnar, correcting a duplicated latitude in the research pool)

stops.name: Porbandar, the Rig Veda that is never finished
stops.date_confidence: attested for the stay and the project; the month is approximate
stops.campa: He stays at Porbandar longer than anywhere else on the road, in the state's guest quarters, working with the Diwan's pandit toward an English translation of Sayana's commentary on the Rig Veda. The pandit tells him his Sanskrit is sufficient, his country too small for him, and that he should go west. The translation is never finished and no manuscript of it is reported anywhere. It is the last time he plans a scholar's life. He leaves Porbandar on the Bombay road.
suggested_refs: The Porbandar state library and guest quarters, Kathiawar
sources: Life of Swami Vivekananda by His Eastern and Western Disciples
The Complete Works of Swami Vivekananda, correspondence

stops.name: Khandwa, the news out of Chicago
stops.date_confidence: attested as a transit stop; the tradition that he first hears of the Parliament here is standard in the order's itineraries and cannot be traced to a contemporaneous document. Day approximate
stops.campa: A transit town in the Central Provinces, on the road between Gujarat and the Bombay Presidency, with nothing in it for a monk. Here, the order's itineraries say, he first hears that a Parliament of Religions will meet at Chicago in 1893 alongside a world's fair. He is twenty-nine and has walked most of India without a plan for any of it. From this point the wandering has a direction, though he tells almost nobody, and he goes on refusing money for the passage until Madras forces it into his hands.
suggested_refs: Khandwa junction, Central Provinces, on the Bombay road

stops.name: Poona, the train journey and Tilak
stops.date_confidence: attested at July 1892 by Wikipedia's travels article; the research pool located this meeting in Bombay and added Justice Ranade, who is not attested in anything reached and has been dropped
stops.campa: On a train in July a Marathi passenger falls into Sanskrit conversation with a Bengali monk and takes him home. Bal Gangadhar Tilak, editor, mathematician, and the coming force of Indian nationalism, keeps him eight days at Poona. Tilak recalls decades afterward that his guest argued religion where he himself argued politics, and that neither of them shifted the other an inch. They part at the end of the week, the one to his newspaper and his politics, the other to the boat.
suggested_refs: Tilak's house at Poona; Tilak's later reminiscence of the train journey
sources: Recollections attributed to Bal Gangadhar Tilak in Ramakrishna Mission biographies

stops.name: Mysore, the Maharaja's offer of a passage
stops.date_confidence: attested for the reception at Bangalore and Mysore; the sources differ on whether he declines the fare at this point, and the disagreement is not resolved
stops.campa: Received at Bangalore by the Diwan K. Seshadri Iyer, he comes on to the palace at Mysore, where Chamarajendra Wadiyar hears him out and offers to pay his passage to America outright. He declines the fare and takes the letters of introduction. The Maharaja's support arrives later by other routes. In one southern winter he collects the backing of three princely states and a circle of students in Madras, and he is still walking, and he still has no ticket.
suggested_refs: The Mysore palace of Chamarajendra Wadiyar X; the letters of introduction of 1892
sources: Life of Swami Vivekananda by His Eastern and Western Disciples
The Complete Works of Swami Vivekananda, correspondence

stops.name: Kanyakumari, the rock at the end of India
stops.date_confidence: the arrival on foot at Christmas Eve 1892 and the resolve of that winter are attested; the swim to the rock and the three days of meditation are legend, so labelled in Wikipedia's own article on the memorial
stops.campa: He reaches the last land of India on Christmas Eve and sits where three seas meet. The legend has him swim to the offshore rock and meditate there three days and three nights. What he writes to Madras within weeks is arithmetic: India has produced philosophy for three thousand years and cannot feed itself, and religion offered to a starving man is an insult. He will go west to raise money and come back to build an order that feeds people. The order dates itself from this beach.
suggested_refs: The offshore rock at Kanyakumari, later the Vivekananda Rock Memorial; the letters to Alasinga Perumal of early 1893
sources: The Complete Works of Swami Vivekananda, letters to Alasinga Perumal

stops.name: Madurai, the Raja of Ramnad tells him to go
stops.date_confidence: attested for the meeting in January 1893; the order of the southern towns differs between Wikipedia's travels article and the order's biographies and is not resolved here. Day approximate
stops.campa: Under the pillared halls at Madurai he meets Bhaskara Sethupathi, Raja of Ramnad, who tells him to go to Chicago as India's representative and puts money behind it. Wikipedia's itinerary runs Madurai, then Rameswaram, then Pondicherry, then Madras. The order's biographies put Ramnad first and Madurai on the way north. The towns are the same and the sequence is not, and neither account is preferred here. What is fixed is that a Tamil prince gives the Bengali monk his commission.
suggested_refs: The Meenakshi Amman temple at Madurai; the court of Bhaskara Sethupathi of Ramnad
sources: Life of Swami Vivekananda by His Eastern and Western Disciples

stops.name: Adyar and Madras, the subscription raised in the street
stops.date_confidence: attested; the Madras period runs February to May 1893 and the day is defaulted. Pin inherited from the atlas's canonical Adyar coordinate
stops.campa: In Madras a circle of young men with Alasinga Perumal at their head decide the monk is going to Chicago whether he consents or not. They beg door to door through the city for the fare, and he refuses the first collection because it comes from the rich. Downriver at Adyar stands the world headquarters of the Theosophical Society, Blavatsky's foundation and soon Annie Besant's seat, already shipping Hindu doctrine to Europe by another road entirely. The two missions share a city and no organization.
suggested_refs: The Theosophical Society headquarters at Adyar; the Madras subscription letters in the Complete Works
sources: The Complete Works of Swami Vivekananda, letters

stops.name: Bombay, the Peninsular sails east
stops.date_confidence: attested by Wikipedia and the Belur Math chronology. Pin inherited from the atlas's canonical Bombay coordinate
stops.campa: On the thirty-first of May he boards the Peninsular at Bombay, dressed by the Raja of Khetri in ochre silk and a turban, carrying a purse he did not raise himself. He has no invitation to the Parliament, no credentials from any body of Hindus, no letter an American committee will recognize, and no return passage. Fourteen years before, at this port, Blavatsky and Olcott came ashore and kissed the ground, the first Westerners to arrive in India to learn rather than to convert. He is the traffic going the other way.
suggested_refs: The Bombay docks and the steamship Peninsular, 31 May 1893

stops.name: Colombo, the outward call
stops.date_confidence: attested as a port call on the outward voyage; the exact date is not fixed in the sources consulted
stops.campa: The ship calls at Colombo and he goes ashore for a few hours among Ceylon's Buddhists. Blavatsky took the Buddhist five precepts at Kandy in 1880, a Western woman entering an Eastern religion in front of Western witnesses; he is making the mirror crossing, and he will land at this same harbour in 1897 as a national figure met by crowds. On this passage he is an unknown monk in a deck cabin, seasick, writing to Madras about money he has not spent yet.
suggested_refs: Colombo harbour on the eastbound mail route, 1893
sources: Life of Swami Vivekananda by His Eastern and Western Disciples

stops.name: Nagasaki, the first sight of a modern Asia
stops.date_confidence: attested for the Japanese leg in July 1893; the individual port dates are not fixed in the sources consulted
stops.campa: Japan astonishes him. He lands at Nagasaki and goes on to Kobe, Osaka, Kyoto, and Tokyo, writing home about clean streets, wide roads, universal schooling, and a people who have taken the machinery of Europe without kneeling to it. He tells the young men of Madras to come and see it, and to stop believing that crossing the sea costs a man his caste. He is looking at what he wants for India, and he is on his way to ask America to pay for a part of it.
suggested_refs: The letters from Japan in the Complete Works, Volume 5
sources: The Complete Works of Swami Vivekananda, letters from Japan

stops.name: Chicago, the Art Institute and the words of welcome
stops.date_confidence: attested; the coordinate corrects a longitude sign error in the research pool that placed the Art Institute in western China
stops.campa: He arrives in Chicago on the thirtieth of July, learns the Parliament will not open for six weeks and that no delegate is admitted without credentials, runs out of money, sleeps a night in a boxcar in Boston, and is put forward at last by a Harvard professor who hears him talk. On the eleventh of September he rises in the Hall of Columbus, drops the address he has prepared, and opens with a form of words no speaker before him has used. The hall stands. Some accounts give the ovation two minutes and some far longer.
stops.quote: Sisters and Brothers of America, It fills my heart with joy unspeakable to rise in response to the warm and cordial welcome which you have given us.
stops.quote_source: Response to Welcome, Addresses at the Parliament of Religions, The Complete Works of Swami Vivekananda, Vol. 1, delivered 11 September 1893, Chicago
suggested_refs: The Hall of Columbus in the Art Institute of Chicago; the Parliament of Religions proceedings of 1893
sources: The Complete Works of Swami Vivekananda, Vol. 1 (Wikisource)

stops.name: Chicago, the Midway Plaisance and the moving pictures
stops.date_confidence: attested for the fair and for the address of 15 September; the juxtaposition with Muybridge is the atlas's own and rests on shared time and place only. Pin inherited byte-identical from muybridge.journey.json
stops.campa: The Parliament sits inside the World's Columbian Exposition, and a mile south along the Midway Plaisance, Eadweard Muybridge is charging admission at the Zoopraxographical Hall to show photographs of horses and men in motion. Same fair, same season: one man selling the eye a fact it cannot catch unaided, the other selling the ear a religion it has not heard of. Neither exhibit records the other. On the fifteenth Vivekananda tells the Parliament that each faith sits in a well of its own.
stops.quote: I am a Hindu. I am sitting in my own little well and thinking that the whole world is my little well. The Christian sits in his little well and thinks the whole world is his well. The Mohammedan sits in his little well and thinks that is the whole world.
stops.quote_source: Why We Disagree, Addresses at the Parliament of Religions, The Complete Works of Swami Vivekananda, Vol. 1, delivered 15 September 1893, Chicago
suggested_refs: Muybridge's Zoopraxographical Hall on the Midway Plaisance, 1893
sources: The Complete Works of Swami Vivekananda, Vol. 1 (Wikisource)

stops.name: Chicago, the closing session and the missionary societies
stops.date_confidence: attested
stops.campa: He speaks six times more. On the nineteenth he reads a paper on Hinduism and salutes Columbia, motherland of liberty, who never dipped her hand in her neighbour's blood. On the twentieth he tells an assembly of missionary societies that it is an insult to offer religion to a starving man and that they might try saving bodies. On the twenty-seventh the Parliament closes. The American press has made him famous in seventeen days, and the missionary societies in America and in Bengal begin the campaign against him that runs the rest of his life.
stops.quote: You Christians, who are so fond of sending out missionaries to save the soul of the heathen — why do you not try to save their bodies from starvation? ... It is an insult to a starving people to offer them religion; it is an insult to a starving man to teach him metaphysics.
stops.quote_source: Religion not the Crying need of India, Addresses at the Parliament of Religions, The Complete Works of Swami Vivekananda, Vol. 1, delivered 20 September 1893, Chicago
suggested_refs: The final session of the World's Parliament of Religions, 27 September 1893
The Paper on Hinduism of 19 September 1893
sources: The Complete Works of Swami Vivekananda, Vol. 1 (Wikisource)

stops.name: New York, the Vedanta Society
stops.date_confidence: attested for the founding in 1894; the month is not fixed in the sources consulted and is approximate
stops.campa: For a year he lectures for fees across the American Midwest and East, is handled by a bureau he comes to loathe, and is accused in the Detroit papers and the Calcutta ones of eating forbidden food and of being no monk at all. He writes to Alasinga that miracles are nonsense and that Ramakrishna must be written up as a life, not a conjuring act. In 1894 he founds the Vedanta Society of New York. Blavatsky founded the Theosophical Society in this same city nineteen years earlier, two imports and one appetite.
stops.quote: What nonsense about the miracle of Ramakrishna! ... Miracles I do not know nor understand. Had Ramakrishna nothing to do in the world but turning wine into the Gupta's medicine? Lord save me from such Calcutta people!
stops.quote_source: Letter XXII to Alasinga Perumal, Epistles - First Series, The Complete Works of Swami Vivekananda, Vol. 5, dated 30 November 1894
suggested_refs: The first rooms of the Vedanta Society of New York, 1894
sources: The Complete Works of Swami Vivekananda, Vol. 5 (Wikisource)

stops.name: Thousand Island Park, the seven weeks in the cottage
stops.date_confidence: attested for the retreat of June to August 1895; the day is defaulted
stops.campa: In a cottage above the St Lawrence, lent by a student, he keeps twelve people for seven weeks and talks without notes, without a platform, and without the lecture bureau. Two of them write down what he says and it is printed later as Inspired Talks. He initiates his first Western monastics here. He writes from this porch that he is finished with fame and with organizations and wants to be left alone with a few, and he then spends the seven years remaining founding institutions on two continents.
stops.quote: May the Lord bless you and yours for ever and ever is the constant prayer of Vivekananda.
stops.quote_source: Letter XLV, 'Mother' (Mrs. Betty Sturges), Epistles - First Series, The Complete Works of Swami Vivekananda, Vol. 5, Thousand Island Park, July 1895
suggested_refs: Miss Dutcher's cottage at Thousand Island Park, New York; the text of Inspired Talks
sources: The Complete Works of Swami Vivekananda, Vol. 5 (Wikisource)

stops.name: London, the classes and Margaret Noble
stops.date_confidence: attested for the meeting with Margaret Noble in November 1895; the research pool's claim of two UK visits both in 1896 is corrected to 1895 and 1896. Pin inherited from the atlas's canonical London coordinate
stops.campa: He crosses to England twice, in 1895 and again in 1896, and finds the London audience harder and steadier than the American: fewer converts, better questions. He lectures from rented rooms and private houses, among them E. T. Sturdy's at Wimbledon. In a drawing room in November an Irish schoolmistress named Margaret Elizabeth Noble comes to argue and stays to learn; she follows him to Calcutta as Sister Nivedita. Annie Besant is working the same city on neighbouring subjects, from another address and another lineage.
suggested_refs: E. T. Sturdy's house at Wimbledon; the London Vedanta classes of 1895 and 1896
sources: Life of Swami Vivekananda by His Eastern and Western Disciples

stops.name: Oxford, lunch at 7 Norham Gardens
stops.date_confidence: attested; pin inherited byte-identical from max_muller.journey.json
stops.campa: Max Muller invites him to lunch at 7 Norham Gardens on the twenty-eighth of May and shows him the proofs of an essay on Ramakrishna. The old philologist, who has translated the Vedas without ever setting foot in India, questions the monk about a Bengali temple priest ten years dead, and Vivekananda leaves saying the Englishman is a Vedantist. Muller expands the essay into a book in 1898, the first substantial portrait of Ramakrishna in a European language. Paul Deussen he meets separately, at Kiel, in Germany, not in England.
suggested_refs: Max Muller's house at 7 Norham Gardens, Oxford
Max Muller, Ramakrishna, His Life and Sayings (1898)

stops.name: Colombo, the return to Asian ground
stops.date_confidence: attested
stops.campa: The unknown monk of 1893 lands at Colombo on the fifteenth of January to garlands, triumphal arches over the road, processions, and a public address from the Hindus of the city read out to him in the street. The crowds hold up the carriage. The whole return from Colombo to Almora is one continuous tour, and the lectures given on it are printed under that name. From the first platform he uses it to tell India that its religion is not the problem and its treatment of its own poor is.
suggested_refs: The Colombo reception of January 1897; the Colombo to Almora lectures
sources: The Complete Works of Swami Vivekananda, Colombo to Almora lectures

stops.name: Rameswaram, the Raja in the shafts
stops.date_confidence: attested in the order's biographies for January 1897; the day within the month is not fixed
stops.campa: Crossing to the mainland at Pamban he is met by Bhaskara Sethupathi, the Raja of Ramnad who four years earlier told him to go. The Raja unharnesses the horses, takes the shafts himself, and pulls the carriage barefoot toward the Ramanathaswamy temple in front of his own subjects. At the temple Vivekananda tells the assembly that the man who sees Shiva in the poor serves better than the man who sees Shiva only in the image, and that the worship he wants from them is worship of the living.
suggested_refs: The Ramanathaswamy temple at Rameswaram; the Pamban address of January 1897
sources: Life of Swami Vivekananda by His Eastern and Western Disciples
The Complete Works of Swami Vivekananda, Colombo to Almora lectures

stops.name: Triplicane, the ice house on the Madras beach
stops.date_confidence: attested; the research pool attached the name Castle Kernan to the 1842 construction, which is corrected here, and the coordinate is moved about 0.9 km
stops.campa: He lodges from the sixth to the fourteenth of February in a round building on the Madras beach, put up in 1842 by the Boston merchant Frederic Tudor to store ice cut from New England ponds and shipped around the Cape. The ice trade collapsed in 1880; an advocate bought the shell and named it Castle Kernan after a judge he liked. From its verandah the monk addresses crowds too large for any hall in the city. In 1963 the state renames it Vivekanandar Illam; in 1997 it passes to the Ramakrishna Math and opens as a museum.
suggested_refs: Vivekanandar Illam, the former Madras ice house, Triplicane

stops.name: Calcutta, the Ramakrishna Mission constituted
stops.date_confidence: attested by Wikipedia and the Belur Math chronology
stops.campa: On the first of May, at Balaram Bose's house in Calcutta, he calls together the monastic and lay disciples and constitutes the Ramakrishna Mission, its object stated as service: schools, famine relief, plague work, hospitals, and the preaching of Vedanta as one enterprise and not two. He tells the brother monks that a man who will not touch a leper because his own liberation matters more has understood nothing at all. The brotherhood that began in a haunted house at Baranagar acquires bylaws, a committee, and a name.
suggested_refs: Balaram Bose's house, Baghbazar, Calcutta; the founding minutes of 1 May 1897

stops.name: Belur, the land on the west bank
stops.date_confidence: attested for 1898 by the Belur Math chronology; no month given, so day and month default to 01
stops.campa: With money raised in America and England he buys land at Belur on the west bank of the Hooghly, across the water from Dakshineswar, and moves the monastery onto it. In the same year he writes a hymn to Ramakrishna. He describes the temple he wants built there: a plan that reads as a church from one angle, a mosque from another, and a temple from the third, under a dome borrowed from the Renaissance. It is consecrated in 1938, thirty-six years after his death, to the drawings of a brother monk trained as an engineer.
suggested_refs: The Belur land purchase of 1898; the Sri Ramakrishna Temple as designed by Swami Vijnanananda

stops.name: Mayavati, the ashrama that keeps no images
stops.date_confidence: attested at 19 March 1899; the research pool dated the founding to 1897 and placed it about 30 km northeast of the true site, both corrected here
stops.campa: In the Himalayan foothills above Lohaghat, at nineteen hundred metres, Captain James Henry Sevier and Charlotte Sevier found the Advaita Ashrama on the nineteenth of March 1899 at his wish: a house for the study of non-dualism where no image is worshipped, not Kali, not Ramakrishna, not him. It is the one place in his own order where his portrait is refused. Its press prints Prabuddha Bharata and later the nine volumes of his collected works. He visits exactly once, from the third to the eighteenth of January 1901.
suggested_refs: The Advaita Ashrama at Mayavati and its press; Prabuddha Bharata, published since July 1896

segments.name: The Second Crossing and the End

stops.name: San Francisco, the second American year
stops.date_confidence: attested for 1900; the month is not fixed in the sources consulted and is approximate
stops.campa: He sails again in June 1899 with Sister Nivedita and Swami Turiyananda, ill with asthma and diabetes and told by everyone to rest. In California he lectures across the Bay Area, founds the western branch of the Vedanta Society, and collects the students who will pay for a retreat in the hills. He is thirty-seven and looks older. Between platforms he writes to Calcutta about drainage, plague camps, and the price of rice. The Americans in the hall see a philosopher; the letters going home are almost entirely administration.
suggested_refs: The Vedanta Society of Northern California, founded 1900

stops.name: Shanti Ashrama, the valley east of San Jose
stops.date_confidence: attested for 1900; the month is approximate and the coordinate corrects the research pool by about 14 km
stops.campa: A hundred and sixty acres in the upper San Antonio valley, forty miles east of San Jose, dry hills with no road worth the name, are given for a retreat and named Shanti Ashrama. Turiyananda is left to run it, and American students live in tents and study Vedanta through a California summer. It is the forest hermitage transplanted, on land held by people whose grandparents came west for gold. Vivekananda never lives in it. He leaves the country within weeks of its founding and does not come back.
suggested_refs: Shanti Ashrama, upper San Antonio Valley, Santa Clara County
sources: Vedanta Society historical accounts cited in Wikipedia

stops.name: Paris, the Congress and the last European weeks
stops.date_confidence: attested for September 1900; the day is defaulted and the subsequent tour dates are approximate
stops.campa: He addresses the Congress of the History of Religions at the Exposition Universelle, arguing against the European philologists over the dating of the Vedas, and it is the last major platform he takes in the West. Then, hosted by the writer Jules Bois, he moves fast through Vienna, Constantinople, Athens, and Egypt, sightseeing on borrowed strength, his letters visibly exhausted. In Cairo something turns him homeward without explanation. He sails at once, ahead of his own party, and reaches Calcutta on the ninth of December.
suggested_refs: The Congress of the History of Religions, Paris Exposition Universelle, September 1900
sources: The Complete Works of Swami Vivekananda, late letters

stops.name: Belur Math, the last year of work
stops.date_confidence: attested for the return on 9 December 1900; the Belur Math chronology gives the month only
stops.campa: He arrives at Belur at night, unannounced, and walks into the monastery while the monks are at supper. What is left of his health goes on the order's business: the Mayavati journey of January 1901, correspondence with America, the girls' school Nivedita opens in Calcutta, famine and plague relief in Bengal. He hands over the running of the Mission and tells the brother monks he will not see forty. Asthma, diabetes, and sleeplessness appear in his letters beside arrangements for buildings he does not expect to see finished.
suggested_refs: Belur Math in 1901; Sister Nivedita's girls' school at Baghbazar

stops.name: Bodh Gaya, the last pilgrimage
stops.date_confidence: attested for January 1902; the research pool's chronology lens placed this in 1901, which is corrected here, since the January 1901 journey was to Mayavati
stops.campa: In January he goes to the Mahabodhi temple at Bodh Gaya, where the Buddha is said to have sat, and spends his birthday there. From Bodh Gaya he goes on to Varanasi, where fourteen years earlier he told people he would return at the end. In Varanasi he helps found a home for the sick and dying poor and refuses to stay, saying the Bengalis will not let him die anywhere but Belur. He comes back up the river in March. The walking that made him is now done by rail, with an attendant.
suggested_refs: The Mahabodhi Temple at Bodh Gaya; the Varanasi home for the sick and dying poor, founded 1902
sources: Life of Swami Vivekananda by His Eastern and Western Disciples

stops.name: Belur Math, the fourth of July
stops.date_confidence: attested; the medical cause and the order's mahasamadhi framing are both recorded and neither is preferred
stops.campa: He rises early, meditates three hours in the chapel, teaches Sanskrit grammar and the Shukla Yajurveda to the students, walks two miles with a brother monk discussing a Vedic college he wants founded, jokes at supper, and at seven goes to his room and tells the attendant to keep the windows open. At about twenty past nine he lies down, cries out once, and stops breathing. The physicians name a ruptured blood vessel in the brain. The order names mahasamadhi, a yogi's deliberate departure. He is thirty-nine.
suggested_refs: Swami Vivekananda's room at Belur Math, kept as he left it

stops.name: Belur, the sandalwood pyre on the riverbank
stops.date_confidence: attested at the afternoon of 5 July 1902; the research pool's afterlife lens dated the cremation to 4 July, contradicting its own geography lens, and the later date is used
stops.campa: On the afternoon of the fifth his body is burned on a sandalwood pyre on the riverbank at Belur, across the water from the spot where Ramakrishna was cremated sixteen years before. A shrine is raised on the place and consecrated in 1924, an alabaster Om on its upper storey. In 1962, for the centenary of his birth, work begins on a memorial on the rock off Kanyakumari where the legend puts his three days; Catholic fishermen contest the site, holding that a cross stood there, and a judicial inquiry names the rock for him.
suggested_refs: The Swami Vivekananda Temple at Belur Math, consecrated 28 January 1924
The Vivekananda Rock Memorial at Kanyakumari, inaugurated 2 September 1970
